p: Cyrus: To assure the Jews of their deliverance against the great temptations that they would abide, he names the person and the means.
right hand I have held: Because Cyrus would execute the office of a deliverer, God called him his anointed for a time, but after another sort than he called David.
subdue nations before him: To guide him in the deliverance of my people.
crooked places straight: I will take away all impediments and hindrances.
know that I: Not that Cyrus knew God to worship him correctly, but he had a certain particular knowledge as profane men may have of his power, and so was compelled to deliver God's people.
sake: Not for anything that is in you, or for your worthiness.
girded thee: I have given you strength, power and authority.
light: I send peace and war, prosperity and adversity, as in Am 3:6.

righteousness: He comforts the Jews as if he would say, "Though when you look to the heavens and earth for comfort you see nothing now but signs of God's wrath, yet will cause them to bring forth certain tokens of your deliverance, and of the performance of my promise": which is meant by righteousness.
created it: I have appointed Cyrus to this use and purpose.

Woe to him that contendeth with: By this he bridles their impatience, who in adversity and trouble murmur against God, and will not tarry his pleasure: willing that man would match with his like, and not contend against God.
He hath no hands: That is, it is not perfectly made.

of things to come concerning my: Instead of murmuring, humble yourselves and ask what you will for the consolation of my children, and you will be sure of it as you are of these things which are at your command. Some read it with an interrogation, and make it the application of the comparison.
host have I commanded: That is, the stars.
him up in righteousness: That is, Cyrus, that I may show by him the faithfulness of my promise in delivering my people.
price nor reward: Meaning, freely and without ransom, or any grievous condition.
of Egypt: These people were tributaries to the Persians, and so king Artahshashte gave this money toward the building of the temple, Ezr 7:27.
thine: While they were your enemies, they will now honour you and you will rule them: which was accomplished in the time of Christ.

hidest thyself: By this he exhorts the Jews to patience, though their deliverance is deferred for a time: showing that they would not repent their long patience, but the wicked and idolaters will be destroyed.
inhabited: That is, of men, but chiefly of his Church.
in a dark place of the: As do the false gods, who give uncertain answers.
ye that have escaped of the: All you idolaters who though you seem to have worldly dignity yet in God's sight you are vile and abject.
the ends of the earth: He calls the idolaters to repentance, willing them to look on him with the eye of faith.
righteousness: That is, that the thing which I have promise will be faithfully performed.

knee shall bow: The knowledge of God and the true worshipping will be through all the world, Rom 14:11, Phil 2:10 by which he signifies that we must not only serve God in heart, but declare the same also by outward profession.
shall one say: Meaning the faithful will feel and confess this.
incensed against him shall be ashamed: All the contemners of God.
